reason: This text is the Akedah narrative (Genesis 22), depicting God's test of Abraham's faith. God commands Abraham to sacrifice his son Isaac, then ultimately prevents the sacrifice, praises Abraham for his fear of God and faithfulness, and blesses him abundantly with promises of numerous descendants and that his seed will possess the gates of his enemies. The passage contains no expression of divine complaint about the people; rather, it is a narrative of testing, obedience, and blessing.
